texts.facts: Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85283646/ 1 1. The present claim petition arises out of road accident in which one Saraswati aged about 48 years, suffered grievous injuries resulting in amputation of left foot below knee. An application u/s 166 (1) MV Act was accordingly filed by the petitioner. Further, on 06.12.2024, a Detailed Accident Report was also filed by the police. 2. The brief facts of the case are that on 02.07.2024 at about 2 p.m. petitioner Saraswati was walking from Kalkaji Temple towards Nehru Place Flyover to fetch a bus, a gramin seva tempo bearing no.DL-2W-4777 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) came at a high speed, driven in a rash and negligent manner and hit the petitioner. She sustained grievous injury and was rushed to AIIMS Trauma center. During treatment, she underwent surgery for amputation of her left leg below the knee. 3. An FIR No.272/2024 u/s 281/125(b) BNS was registered at PS Kalkaji, New Delhi. Police investigated the matter and filed chargesheet against the driver of the offending vehicle before concerned criminal court while separate claim petition and DAR Digitally was filed before this Tribunal. Charu signed by Charu gupta Date: gupta 2026.01.06 17:28:03 +0530 MACT No. 1477/24 Saraswati v. Saroj Yadav Page no. 2 of 21 BK 4. As per record, the offending vehicle was driven by respondent no.1, owned by respondent no.2 and insured with respondent no.3 and Respondent no.4 is Nodal officer of such company. 5. Matter was adjourned several times for settlement but no settlement could be arrived at. Insurance company filed a legal offer of Rs.18,52,676/- which was declined on the ground that the compensation offered was unjust and unreasonable. Since no statutory defence has been raised by the insurance company, by filing a legal offer, liability to compensate the petitioner has been admitted. The only point of contention is the quantum of compensation. Parties do not wish to lead any evidence and have sought to rely on the documents already on record filed with the claim petition and DAR. 6. As per Mohd. Sabeer case (supra), cost of repair and maintenance has been assessed between 15,000/- to Rs.20,000/-. Further, petitioner has filed medical bills amounting Rs.4317/- and has shown to have been treated in a government hospital. under (vi) 2. texts.arguments: As per decision of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in Rajesh Tyagi & Ors. v. Jaibir Singh & Ors.(FAO No.842/2003, decided on 08.01.2021), wherein it was observed: "...13.10. 9. As regards the quantum of compensation, this court is governed by the law laid down by Honb'le Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680. The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. 10. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) Saraswati vs Saroj Yadav on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85283646/ 3 10.6. Observation of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rajkumar v. Ajay Saraswati vs Saroj Yadav on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85283646/ It has been clarified by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kirti vs Oriental Insurance Company Limited, AIR 2021 SUPREME COURT 353, that a homemaker's income should be generally assessed as that of a skilled worker for compensation purposes. As per judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in Mohd. Sabeer v. UPSRTC (2022 SCC OnLine SC 1701) as referred by Hon'ble Digitally signed by Charu Charu Date: gupta gupta 2026.01.06 17:28:47 +0530 MACT No. 1477/24 Saraswati v. Saroj Yadav Page no. 9 of 21 BK Delhi High Court in judgment of Pavan Paswan v. Ranjit Yadav & Ors. (decided on 19.05.2025), where the victim was 37 years of age with a life expectancy of 70 years, he was awarded as sum of Rs.7,80,000/- towards cost of prosthetic limb assuming replacement of limb every 5 to 6 years. The cost of prosthetic limb for six years has thus been assumed by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mohd. Sabeer Case (supra) to be Rs.1,11,428/-. Further, in view of decision of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in Chander Jeet Singh vs. Mahavir Singh MAC.APP110/2006, this sum awarded to the petitioner is directed to be kept in two fixed deposits of Rs.2,62,856/- each initially for a period of 2 years. On such deposits being made, the insurance company shall submit a letter to the Nazir of this Tribunal enclosing a copy of the said bank advice, in prescribed format as above, as per which the deposit made to the bank account of this Tribunal, to enable this Tribunal to keep tab on the deposits made and the MCOPs for which they were made. The Payment advice for remittance of compensation is as under: PAYMENT ADVICE FOR REMITTANCE COMPENSATION : ............ Bank ................... To: ............... Court ........................ In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". In the case of illiterate claimants, the Tribunal is allowed to consider the request for lumpsum payment for effecting purchase of any movable property such as agricultural implements, rickshaws etc. to earn a living. Moreover, in the case of literate persons, the Tribunal may resort to the procedure indicated in guideline No. (i) only if, having regard to the age, fiscal background and strata of the society to which the claimant belongs and such other considerations, the Tribunal Saraswati vs Saroj Yadav on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85283646/ 12 thinks that in the larger interest of the claimant and with a view to ensure the safety of the compensation awarded, it is necessary to invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit.
